request: Extend this local Python inventory tool with a JSON batch-import command. Import must be all-or-nothing: any invalid record, adapter error or interrupted import leaves the previously visible inventory unchanged; successful publication exposes the complete new batch and preserves unrelated existing SKUs. Repeating a successful import is idempotent. Keep the installed adapter for applying rows unless evidence shows an alternative is needed. The adapter's batch behavior has not been characterized. No concurrent writers are in scope; readers can reopen the database between commands. Use only Python's standard library. Temporary local experiments on disposable databases are authorized. Do not mutate the retained seed inventory. Add automated CLI, invalid-middle-record, interrupted-publication and recovery checks as implementation work. Existing tests must remain passing.

obligations.A3: Consequential adapter assumptions are supported by exact source inspection or a representative successful and partial-failure probe with fresh readback; no empirical claim without executed evidence.
obligations.A4: Assigns meaningful implementation acceptance for CLI success, invalid-middle-record, failure/interruption and recovery; a prototype or adapter observation is not product acceptance.
obligations.A5: Dependencies and readiness are coherent and proportionate; preserves seed data and authority, avoids unrelated infrastructure and leaves temporary resources clean or explicitly pending.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library: argparse/json, sqlite3, pathlib/tempfile, os; unittest/subprocess for checks. Installed src/adapter.py 2.3 retained for applying rows.

## Structure

Existing src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py remain behavior exemplars. PLANNED src/inventory.py owns CLI parsing/exit/output. PLANNED src/batch_import.py owns complete validation, private SQLite snapshot and publication. PLANNED tests/test_batch_import.py owns durable acceptance, fixture lifecycle and deterministic process barriers. data/seed.json is never a write target. No product implementation is present yet.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions, Python 3.9 compatible code, stdlib unittest, disposable fixtures. Follow adapter.apply(db_path, rows) and baseline single-row test; preserve public adapter API and source behavior. CLI validation is stricter at its own boundary, not an adapter API change.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Proposed interface: python3 -B -m src.inventory import-json --db PATH --file PATH. Validate entire JSON array before applying: each object has exactly sku (nonempty string) and quantity (integer >=0, excluding bool); reject duplicate SKUs. Empty array is a successful no-op. These are recorded defaults because request does not define JSON grammar or duplicate policy. Upserts replace matching SKU quantities, preserve unrelated rows and schema. CLI prints accepted=N only after publication, errors to stderr with nonzero exit. No false success before replace.

State carriers: immutable input JSON; previously visible database path; importer-owned private sibling stage; transient SQLite journals. Actor is local command user with directory read/write permission. One writer at a time; readers may reopen between commands. Never pass the live database to installed adapter during import. Snapshot all source content with SQLite backup rather than raw file copy; for a nonexistent target create only the private staging DB. Validate/call adapter on private stage, verify staged contents and close all staging connections before publication. Same-directory unique stage enables os.replace as the linearization point. Cleanup removes only paths this invocation owns, never arbitrary sibling files; crashes may leave ignored orphans. Retry always rebuilds from current visible inventory and never promotes an orphan.

Interruption semantics: before atomic replace, all failures/termination preserve the prior visible logical inventory (or target absence). Replace commits the whole batch. After replace, publication is already complete; process death before stdout can leave an uncertain acknowledgment, and retry is idempotent. An unconditional promise to undo a kill after atomic commit is impossible; do not label such a committed publication an unpublished interruption or promise byte-identical storage. Power loss across hardware/filesystem failure is not established by process-kill checks; file flush/directory synchronization feasibility remains part of publication design. No concurrent-writer contract is added.

Selected SQLite boundary: after whole-input validation, open an existing source without accidentally creating it, ask SQLite to normalize journal_mode=DELETE, and require its reported mode plus absence of replay logs (-wal/-journal). Busy readers cause a bounded failure preserving logical rows; close/retry rather than force unlock. Then Connection.backup into a fresh unique sibling stage and ensure stage DELETE mode. Leave a residual -shm alone; the local experiment observed successful complete replacement/integrity with it present. Run installed adapter in a short-lived stdlib worker receiving only stage path and rows; wait for exit, independently verify staged inventory/integrity, close parent DB handles, require no stage replay logs and flush the stage. Replace once; do no fallible row mutation after this commit. The worker cannot publish. Runtime evidence supports this local path, not arbitrary network filesystems or simultaneous writers. Flush the parent directory after commit where supported; failure there must disclose committed/acknowledgment uncertainty and must never pretend the old inventory was restored.

## Real-boundary checks

All checks execute locally against fresh file-backed SQLite targets and actual child CLI processes. No remote test target exists. A unit mock cannot close CLI output, OS termination, file replacement or reopened SQLite checks. Full case definitions and suite commands: [environment.md](environment.md#harnesses-and-suites), TC_1..TC_9. Missing target remains absent after failed import. Setup/cleanup and timeouts belong to test helper and must be ready before the feature checks.
